title: Start with the school, not the product.
standfirst: The right context, at the point it matters.
summary: Understand individual schools, trusts and the wider sector — so you can identify need and make every interaction more relevant.
lead: Education IQ helps organisations understand individual schools, trusts and the wider education sector so they can identify need, make every interaction more relevant and build better relationships with educators.

blocks.title: What people use it for
blocks.lead: Education IQ is not a feature list. It is a set of questions organisations need answered.

items.title: Understand individual schools
items.body: Who they are, how they’re structured, what’s changing and what that might mean.

items.title: Understand trusts
items.body: How a trust is composed, where decisions sit, and which schools sit inside it.

items.title: Identify likely need
items.body: Find the organisations whose circumstances suggest they need what you do.

items.title: Analyse your customers
items.body: Understand the organisations you already serve — and what they have in common.

items.title: Find opportunities across trusts
items.body: You serve four schools in a trust of nineteen. Now what?

items.title: Identify risk
items.body: Leadership change, financial pressure, structural change — before renewal.

items.title: Find lookalikes
items.body: Find organisations that resemble your strongest customers.

items.title: Improve targeting
items.body: Fewer, better-aimed conversations rather than more of them.

items.title: Enrich your CRM
items.body: Put education context next to the records your team already works in.

blocks.text: Works with the CRM you’ve already got.
blocks.sub: Salesforce, HubSpot, Microsoft Dynamics or something else entirely. Your technology doesn’t need our logo on it.

blocks.title: Data is the foundation. Intelligence is the product.
paras: Knowing who exists is useful. Knowing who matters is better. Education IQ exists to close that gap — and where it helps, to put a person alongside the data who can tell you what it means.

testimonialTheme: EdCo understanding both education and the client’s business

title: From digital brochure to education engagement platform.
standfirst: Schools don’t need more vendors. They need partners. EdNet sites help suppliers become one.
summary: A website that demonstrates why schools should want to work with you, rather than listing what you sell.

blocks.title: Most supplier websites are built backwards
paras: Schools buy solutions to problems, not products from suppliers. A conventional supplier website usually begins: who we are → what we sell → why we’re good → contact us.
An EdNet website behaves differently: your challenges → useful help → expertise → engagement → relationship → solution.

blocks.title: What an EdNet site lets you give
Anonymous traffic becomes a known relationship
blocks.lead: EdNet is built to move visitors along a path, and to show you who is walking it.

blocks.text: Give value. Build trust. Understand need. Create relationships.

paras: Your website can sell what you do. Or it can demonstrate why schools should want to work with you.

title: An education CRM without the enterprise headache.
standfirst: SPIRIT is an option, not an agenda.
summary: A fully managed, education-specific CRM — for organisations that want one. If you already have a CRM you like, we’ll work with that instead.

blocks.title: What SPIRIT offers
items: Strong support for selling across trusts

blocks.title: And if you already have a CRM?
paras: Then keep it. If your organisation already uses Salesforce, HubSpot, Microsoft Dynamics or anything else it gets on with, EdCo will help make that environment more valuable rather than argue with it.
SPIRIT is the right answer when an organisation wants a simpler, fully managed, education-specific CRM. It is not the right answer for everyone, and we won’t pretend otherwise.

title: A community of international-school educators.
standfirst: Part of how organisations reach international educators — and part of how EdCo keeps listening to them.
summary: ISN serves international-school educators, and gives organisations a credible route to engage with them.

blocks.title: It is also part of our listening infrastructure
paras: ISN is not only a distribution route. It is one of the places EdCo finds out what international educators are actually dealing with — which is what makes it useful to organisations in the first place.

title: Where EdCo meets UK educators.
standfirst: A resource for educators, and a way for organisations to give value and build relationships.
summary: The Curriculum Network connects EdCo with UK educators through webinars, CPD, research, events and content.

paras: It works in both directions. Educators get things worth their time. Organisations get a credible reason to be in the room. And EdCo keeps hearing, first-hand, what UK educators are dealing with.
